explanations.answer: An angel of the Lord came down from heaven
explanations.explanation: That's the cause. Matthew says, “Suddenly there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven…” The shaking and the angel arrive together. Then the angel rolls the stone away and sits on it.

explanations.answer: The guards were breaking open the seal
explanations.explanation: The guards aren't breaking anything, friend. Verse 4 says they trembled and became like dead men, so they're the ones getting shaken. The earthquake comes because an angel of the Lord descended from heaven. Nobody was cracking that seal.

explanations.answer: A storm was rolling in over the city
explanations.explanation: No storm is mentioned anywhere in this passage. The text gives the cause: “…for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven…” That's one forecast no weather app was ever going to catch. When Matthew explains the shaking, he points to the angel.

That's right. The angel descends from heaven, rolls away the stone, and sits on it. He doesn't just move it, he takes a seat on it. Matthew tells us the stone is gone from the entrance, and the angel is perched on top.
The text says the opposite. The angel of the Lord descended from heaven, rolled away the stone, and sat on it. So the stone doesn't stay where it was. It gets moved, and the angel sits on it.

explanations.answer: They tremble and become like dead men
explanations.explanation: Yes. Matthew says the guards trembled in fear of him and became like dead men. These were the ones posted to watch the tomb, and they go still as stones. That tells you how big this moment was.

explanations.answer: They draw their swords and charge him
explanations.explanation: Matthew doesn't show any swords. The text says the guards trembled in fear and became like dead men. Nobody charges anybody in this scene. They're too shaken to move.

explanations.answer: They bow down and worship the angel
explanations.explanation: The guards don't worship him. Matthew says they trembled in fear of him and became like dead men. The worship in this passage comes later, when the women meet Jesus and worship Him (Matthew 28:9).

explanations.answer: He has risen just as He said
explanations.explanation: That's the news. The angel says, “He is not here; He has risen, just as He said!” Jesus had told His disciples that He would be killed and on the third day be raised to life (Matthew 16:21). So the angel is pointing back to what Jesus already said.

explanations.answer: He was moved to another tomb
explanations.explanation: The angel doesn't say anything about a move. He says, “He is not here; He has risen…” Jesus isn't in a different tomb. He is risen.

explanations.answer: He has gone to the temple courts
explanations.explanation: The angel never mentions the temple courts. His message is that Jesus has risen, just as He said. He then sends the women to tell the disciples, and says Jesus is going ahead of them into Galilee.
The angel says the opposite, friend. He invites the women in with, “Come, see the place where He lay.” They aren't told to stay away. They're told to look.
That's right. The angel says, “Come, see the place where He lay.” So they're invited to come and look, not to keep their distance. Then he sends them off to tell the disciples.

Galilee it is. The angel tells the women to say that Jesus has risen from the dead and is going ahead of the disciples into Galilee. Then he adds, “There you will see Him.” He even finishes with, “See, I have told you.”
Jerusalem isn't the place the angel names. He says Jesus is going ahead of the disciples into Galilee. That's where they will see Him.
The angel doesn't name Bethany. The message for the disciples is that Jesus is going ahead of them into Galilee. That's the place where they will see Him.
Joy it is. Matthew says they hurried away from the tomb in fear and great joy. Both feelings are packed into one run. And they ran to tell His disciples.

Sorrow isn't in the verse. Matthew says the women left the tomb in fear and great joy. That makes sense after hearing that Jesus has risen. I think my oven timer scares me less than that morning scared them.
Matthew doesn't say confusion. He says they hurried away in fear and great joy. They also ran to tell the disciples, so I think they knew exactly what to do next.
Yes, Jesus Himself. Matthew says, “Suddenly Jesus met them and said, ‘Greetings!’” The women were still on their way to tell the disciples when it happened. They didn't have to wait to see Him.
It's not the angel this time. The angel had already spoken to them at the tomb. On the way, the one who meets them is Jesus.
Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, isn't the one who meets them. The women were running to tell the disciples. The one who meets them on the way is Jesus.

explanations.answer: They grasp His feet and worship Him
explanations.explanation: That's what they do. Matthew says they came to Him, grasped His feet, and worshiped Him. They don't hang back. They go right up to Him.

explanations.answer: They run back to the empty tomb
explanations.explanation: They don't run anywhere. Jesus says, “Greetings!” and they come to Him. Matthew says they grasped His feet and worshiped Him.

explanations.answer: They stand back and stay silent
explanations.explanation: The text shows the opposite, friend. The women come to Jesus, grasp His feet, and worship Him. They don't stand back. They go straight to Him.
True. Jesus says, “Go and tell My brothers to go to Galilee.” Notice what He calls them. After everything that happened, they are still His brothers.
It's true, friend. Jesus says, “Go and tell My brothers to go to Galilee. There they will see Me.” That's the name He uses for the disciples in His message.

That's it. After the chief priests had met with the elders and formed a plan, they gave the soldiers a large sum of money. Then they told the soldiers what to say. I think a plan that needs that much cash has a problem.
Matthew doesn't mention a new post. The chief priests give the soldiers a large sum of money. Then they tell them what to say.

No written order is mentioned. Pilate was the Roman governor (Matthew 27:2), and the chief priests actually say they'll deal with him if the report reaches him. What they hand the soldiers is a large sum of money.

Asleep is the word. The chief priests tell them to say, “His disciples came by night and stole Him away while we were asleep.” That's the story they were handed. It's the report they were told to give.
They aren't told to say they were away. The line is “…while we were asleep.” The chief priests chose the story, and asleep is the word in it.
Outnumbered isn't in the instructions. The chief priests tell the soldiers to say the disciples stole Him away while the soldiers were asleep. That's the exact word Matthew gives.
True. The chief priests tell the soldiers, “If this report reaches the governor, we will satisfy him and keep you out of trouble.” So the soldiers get cash and a promise. That's the whole deal.

The text says they do make that promise. The chief priests say, “If this report reaches the governor, we will satisfy him and keep you out of trouble.” So the soldiers are promised protection if the governor hears about it.
Matthew says the opposite. The guards took the money and did as they were instructed. They don't turn it down. They go along with the plan.
That's right. Matthew says, “So the guards took the money and did as they were instructed.” They accepted the money and then told the story the chief priests gave them.
Not quite, friend. Matthew says, “When they saw Him, they worshiped Him, but some doubted.” So worship is there, but doubt is there too. Not all of them are without it.
That's right. Matthew says, “When they saw Him, they worshiped Him, but some doubted.” So there was worship, and there was also doubt among some of them. Jesus comes to them anyway.

explanations.answer: All authority in heaven and on earth
explanations.explanation: Yes. Jesus says, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.” That's the opening of what He tells the eleven. Everything He says after it rests on that.

explanations.answer: A throne in the city of Jerusalem
explanations.explanation: Jesus doesn't mention a throne or a city. He says, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.” That reaches a lot farther than one city.

explanations.answer: Rest from all His work on earth
explanations.explanation: Rest isn't what Jesus says. He tells the eleven, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.” And right after that, He sends them out.
That's the reach. Jesus says, “Therefore go and make disciples of all nations…” That's a big field, and it starts with the eleven standing on that mountain.
Jesus doesn't limit it to Israel. He says, “Therefore go and make disciples of all nations…” The word is all.
The eleven are standing in Galilee, but Jesus doesn't stop there. He says, “Therefore go and make disciples of all nations…” That goes far past one region.

Baptize is the first one. Jesus says to make disciples, “baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit…” That's the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit named together in one line.
Teach is the second one. Jesus says to make disciples, “…and teaching them to obey all that I have commanded you.” It's about obeying all He commanded.
Jesus doesn't say test. The words are baptizing and teaching. There's no quiz in His instructions.
Judge isn't in His instructions. Jesus tells the eleven to baptize and to teach. Those are the two jobs He names.
Count isn't one of the jobs. Jesus tells the eleven to baptize and to teach. I'd lose count of my own cookies anyway, so I'm glad it's not on the list.

explanations.answer: Always to the end of the age
explanations.explanation: That's the promise. Jesus says, “And surely I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” There's no gap in it. He doesn't say when that end comes, and neither do I.

explanations.answer: Until they reach every last nation
explanations.explanation: Jesus doesn't set a finish line like that. He says, “And surely I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” His promise runs through the whole time, not just until a task is done.

explanations.answer: Until their work in Galilee is done
explanations.explanation: Galilee isn't the limit. Jesus has just sent them to all nations. Then He says, “And surely I am with you always, even to the end of the age.”
